faqs.question: How does continuous CPC differ from batch CPC?
faqs.answer: Instead of separate batch runs, sample is injected continuously into two interconnected rotors and less-retained and more-retained compounds exit at opposite ends. This continuous-injection mode gives 3× higher productivity than batch processing, with lower operating costs and no need for frequent restarts.

faqs.question: What is dual-mode (MDM) operation?
faqs.answer: MDM alternates ascending and descending modes, reversing the flow and which liquid phase is mobile. Because partition coefficients are reciprocal, each mode moves a different compound faster, which helps separate compounds with similar partition coefficients.

faqs.question: What are the key numbers?
faqs.answer: Two linked 2.2 L GMP-rCPC rotors (4.4 L rotor volume), 500 mL/min flow rate, continuous sample injection at 300 mL/min, hundreds of grams to kilogram scale per cycle, and four built-in pumps.

faqs.question: What productivity gain can I expect?
faqs.answer: In a red clover alkaloid remediation case study, continuous CPC delivered a threefold increase in productivity versus batch. Isomer work reached 95 % purity (66 %/58 % yields) and a rare isomer exceeded 99 % purity by dual-mode operation.

faqs.question: Is it GMP-grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is designed for pharma GMP (EudraLex Vol. 4) and ATEX Zone 2, holds CE, UKCA and UL/CSA/NRTL certifications and supports validated cleaning procedures.

faqs.question: How does it relate to the iCPC?
faqs.answer: The Continuous CPC (4.4 L, 500 mL/min) handles hundreds of grams to kilogram scale per cycle with continuous injection. The iCPC (23 L, 800–5000 mL/min) handles kilograms per cycle with integrated solvent preparation and recycling.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Centrifugal Partition Chromatography (CPC) is a preparative liquid–liquid technique: two immiscible liquids act as the phases, one held stationary in a rotor by centrifugal force while the other is pumped through. There is no silica gel and no solid stationary phase, which eliminates sample loss and irreversible adsorption. The Continuous CPC runs this as a continuous process rather than a sequence of separate batch runs.

The system is a dual-mode, dual-rotor CPC platform: two GMP-rCPC units with synchronized control and four built-in pumps that alternate ascending and descending modes in a continuous cycle. Sample can be injected at the front of the rotors, which lengthens the column, or between them for uninterrupted injection, and less-retained and more-retained compounds exit at opposite ends. The result is 3× higher productivity than batch processing, reduced solvent consumption with effective recycling, and lower operating costs.

faqs.answer: CPC is a preparative liquid–liquid chromatography technique. Two immiscible liquids form the phases: one is held stationary in a rotor by centrifugal force and the other is pumped through. Compounds separate by how they partition between the two liquids — there is no solid stationary phase.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Centrifugal Partition Chromatography (CPC) is a preparative liquid–liquid chromatography technique. Instead of a packed solid column, it uses two immiscible liquid phases: one is held stationary inside a rotor by centrifugal force while the other is pumped through as the mobile phase. Compounds separate according to how they partition between the two liquids. Because there is no solid stationary phase, sample loss and irreversible adsorption are eliminated, and consumable costs and solvent waste are reduced.

The CPC Modeler packages this into a compact, desktop-sized platform built for method development and as an entry-level system for production scale-up. Its 250 mL rotor and 1–50 mL/min flow handle milligram-to-gram purifications, while the included CPC Simulator lets you model the purification strategy first. Methods then move to production using the same CPC technology, without changing the method.

faqs.answer: It has a 23 L rotor — the world's largest commercially available CPC instrument — and runs at 800–5000 mL/min, processing up to 1200 g per cycle, 20 kg per day and hundreds of kilograms of crude input material per month.

faqs.question: How is it controlled?
faqs.answer: By a PLC (Programmable Logic Controller), which ensures precise parameter tuning, allows integration with multiple devices and supports real-time process automation.

faqs.question: What does the integrated solvent system do?
faqs.answer: It provides fully automated solvent preparation, recovery and regeneration, reclaiming up to 90% of solvents from both mobile and stationary phases and reducing waste and operational expenses.

faqs.question: Can I run several units together?
faqs.answer: Yes. The PLC-controlled automation system can synchronize and manage multiple skids in real time, including multiple purification lines, integrated solvent handling units or additional process modules.

faqs.question: Will my pilot method transfer to the iCPC?
faqs.answer: Yes. The iCPC keeps the same relative resolution and load efficiency as the pilot-scale rCPC, so workflows developed on the rCPC transfer directly without revalidating the purification strategy.

faqs.question: How does it compare to the Continuous CPC?
faqs.answer: The iCPC (23 L, 800–5000 mL/min) handles up to 1200 g per cycle in continuous-batch operation with integrated solvent recycling. The Continuous CPC (4.4 L, 500 mL/min) uses two GMP-rCPC rotors with continuous sample injection for hundreds of grams to kilogram scale per cycle.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Centrifugal Partition Chromatography (CPC) is a preparative liquid–liquid technique: two immiscible liquids act as the phases, one held stationary in a rotor by centrifugal force while the other is pumped through. There is no silica gel and no solid stationary phase, which eliminates sample loss and irreversible adsorption. At industrial scale, the iCPC reduces waste and operational expenses.

The iCPC applies CPC at full production scale. A 23 L rotor and 800–5000 mL/min flow give it the capacity to process hundreds of kilograms of crude input material per month, with 20 kg per day in continuous-batch operation and loading of up to 1200 g per cycle. A PLC ensures precise parameter tuning, integration with multiple devices and real-time process automation, while a fully automated solvent-handling system prepares, recovers and regenerates solvent. Because the iCPC keeps the same relative resolution and load efficiency as the pilot-scale rCPC, workflows developed on the rCPC transfer directly without revalidating the purification strategy.

sections.title: 01 — Product Information
body: Centrifugal Partition Chromatography (CPC) is a preparative liquid–liquid technique: two immiscible liquids act as the phases, one held stationary in a rotor by centrifugal force while the other is pumped through. Compounds separate by how they partition between the liquids. With no solid stationary phase, sample loss and irreversible adsorption are eliminated, and no expensive silica gel or resin is needed.

The GMP-rCPC applies this at pilot scale. A 2.2 L rotor and 100–300 mL/min flow handle grams to hundreds of grams per cycle in ascending and descending modes, and the system is scale-up-ready for at-line use. It is built for regulated manufacturing: it complies with cGMP, EudraLex Volume 4, 21 CFR Part 11 and GAMP 5, supports EN 10204 3.1 material traceability, has FDA-grade wetted parts and holds CE, UKCA and UL/CSA/NRTL certifications. Multiple units can run in parallel, or two units in a loop for continuous processing, under RotaChrom's Adaptive Control System.
